text:
Roman Kantserov came over from Magnitogorsk this fall after 36 goals in 63 KHL games, and he has brought the scoring touch with him. The 44th pick in 2023 has nine goals in his first 21 NHL games, already a pace well above what forwards drafted around him usually manage in a first season. He is quick (96th percentile top speed by NHL Edge) and plays on both Chicago's top line and its top power-play unit.

The caution is loud, though. Nine goals on 4.7 expected (the quality of his chances) means he's shooting 28%, and that rarely holds. The underlying play is harder: Chicago has just 38% of the expected goals at five on five with him on the ice. The goals have also dried up lately, none in his last four games.

His season now gets more weight. With Connor Bedard out with a shoulder injury and the Blackhawks weighing rehab against surgery, Kantserov loses his centre on the top line. Watch whether he can keep getting to his spots without him.
